protocol.py: 3 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 50 ul is below what the p1000_single_gen2 can measure (100 ul at
least)
   line 40:  p1000.aspirate(50, serum_well)
   At line 40 the p1000_single_gen2 is asked to draw 50 ul, below its minimum of 100 ul
   (this line did it 24 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the
   wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The
   simulator passes the move. Wells: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in
   slot 1.
   Affected: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [5c9b76560390]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: pbs (well A1 in slot 2)
   line 44:  p1000.aspirate(450, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 44 the tip went into pbs (well A1 in slot 2) while it still carried serum 1 (tube
   A1 in slot 1), serum 5 (tube A2 in slot 1), serum 2 (tube B1 in slot 1), serum 3 (tube C1
   in slot 1) and 1 more from an earlier step (this line did it 5 times). A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted
   material along into 12 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1 and E1 in slot 3; wells C1, D1, E1,
   F1, G1, H1, I1 and J1 in slot 4.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 12 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1 and E1 in slot 3; wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1,
   H1, I1 and J1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 44 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing

findings.title: 50 ul is below what the p1000_single_gen2 can measure (100 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 40 the p1000_single_gen2 is asked to draw 50 ul, below its minimum of 100 ul (this line did it 24 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: pbs (well A1 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 44 the tip went into pbs (well A1 in slot 2) while it still carried serum 1 (tube A1 in slot 1), serum 5 (tube A2 in slot 1), serum 2 (tube B1 in slot 1), serum 3 (tube C1 in slot 1) and 1 more from an earlier step (this line did it 5 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 12 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1 and E1 in slot 3; wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1, H1, I1 and J1 in slot 4.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 44 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
